newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Parliament cannot oust Yeltsin for illness -report.
newsitem.headline: Parliament cannot oust Yeltsin for illness -report.

text.p: Parliamentary efforts to oust Russian President Boris Yeltsin on health grounds do not have any legal force, the legal department of the State Duma ruled on Wednesday.
But communist deputy Viktor Ilyukhin, who raised the motion on Tuesday, told reporters he would still press for a vote on the issue on Friday.
The legal department of the lower house said that a resolution seeking Yeltsin's removal "cannot have any legal consequences".
Ilyukhin said the legal department's opinion was not binding on deputies and pledged to forge ahead.
The department suggested that instead of voting on Ilyukhin's motion, parliament should rather produce a law clarifying the very hazy constitutional position on removing an ailing head of state.

The constitution says only that the president "ceases his functions" if his health is too weak to remain in office. It does not specify who decides the president is too ill or who makes the final decision that he must step down.
Yeltsin, 65, must spend the rest of the week in hospital with pneumonia, the Kremlin's chief doctor said on Wednesday. In November, Yeltsin underwent quintuple heart bypass surgery.

Gennady Zyuganov, the leader of Russia's Communists, the largest group in the Duma, said on Wednesday the party would decide on Thursday whether to back Ilyukhin's proposal to seek Yeltsin's removal on health grounds.

Ilyukhin said he would seek to have the motion placed on Friday's agenda at a meeting of Duma business managers on Thursday. If he failed, he proposed to put the motion personally to a vote on Friday morning.
